data.title: Predicting Starknet’s next short-term price target after STRK hits 4-month high
data.description:
The altcoin market is in the middle of a trend reversal right now after a period of prolonged weakness. Starknet is no exception to the same. In fact, after STRK successfully held $0.03, the altcoin hiked and flipped $0.04, before hitting $0.046. In doing so, it reached its May 2026 levels.

At the time of writing, STRK was trading at $0.040 following a hike of 31% on the daily charts. Its trading volume saw a record-breaking jump too, with the same up by a whooping 718%. This hinted at greater market participation across the board. 

Here, it’s worth noting that this market activity seemed to be mostly on the buy side. Coinank data revealed that Daily Turnover had jumped to a yearly high of $6.6 million, hinting at greater buying pressure.

A look at Starknet’s recovery

As the market rebounded, Starknet [STRK] investors returned with strength. On 18th September, for instance, the protocol’s capital inflows climbed to $61.7 million.

USD Inflows on Starknet Bridge have not hit these levels since November 2025. Previously, when protocol inflows were hitting such a level, STRK was on a strong upside run while trading at around $0.28.

On top of that, open market demand also seemed to echo this market shift. In fact, over the past 4 days, the altcoin’s Spot Netflows have remained negative.

On 19th September, Netflows dropped to -$1.34 million for the first tume since April. A look at both USD inflows and exchange flows revealed that when both reached press time levels previously, Starknet performed well on the price charts.

Is there reason to worry though?

Despite growing market optimism and capital flows, the crypto community has some concerns with STRK. Especially since some on-chain monitors have raised concerns over team-linked wallet dumping. 

According to Arsian, over the past month, team-linked wallets have sold every time the token recorded some gains. In its latest move, team-linked wallets received 17 million STRK and started depositing to exchanges.

At first , the wallet deposited 4 million STRK into Binance. Often, these deposits have followed dumping based on previous patterns. Such market behavior, especially from the team, tends to increase supply, which also precedes market weakness.

Additionally, new supply is anticipated to hit the market, according to Miau. The analyst noted that 175M tokens will likely increase new supply, resulting in a new fight between renewed demand and fresh supply.

These two aspects are likely to cause market pressure and risk the prevailing trend’s sustainability.

Can STRK hold the uptrend?

Regardless of the highlighted concerns, the market was leaning bullish at press time. STRK’s price was sitting above its short-term and long-term moving averages, reflecting strong upside pressure.

At the same time, Starknet’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) sat deep in the bullish zone at around 66.

Together, these trend indicators hinted at the likelihood of a trend continuation. Therefore, if the demand can hold, STRK will reclaim $0.046 and target a flip of $0.05. For this outlook to hold, STRK must close above $0.041. Failure to do so, and the altcoin could revisit $0.03 support.

Final Summary

  • Starknet [STRK] surged by 31% and flipped $0.04-resistance to hit a four-month high of $0.046.
  • Starknet’s rally driven by strong market demand and improving market sentiment.

data.title: President Trump or Coinbase’s Armstrong — Who’s really responsible for CLARITY Act failure?
data.description:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong has distanced himself from claims by the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) that he was responsible for the CLARITY Act’s failure. 

The much-awaited and crucial crypto legislation hit a snag earlier in the week after it failed to clear a procedural vote to advance to the Senate floor debate. 

No Democrats supported the bill, citing limited ethics provisions. A handful of Republicans also withheld support, bringing the vote tally to 49 (Yes)-50 (No), which fell short of the 60 votes needed to advance the bill.

However, the WSJ is reportedly planning to pin the failure on Armstrong. In response, Armstrong stated, 

In January, I opposed a draft of the bill going into a committee vote because it needed a lot of work on DeFi, tokenization, CFTC authority, and stablecoin rewards. At the time, the bill had major issues that would have harmed crypto.

At the time, even the White House scolded his opposition and warned that he’s not the crypto industry. However, he insisted that he’s “proud” of his opposition because it led to a “better bill.”

On the revised version, which had a stablecoin yield compromise, Armstrong added, 

The final draft of CLARITY that went to the Senate was great, and I strongly supported it. It’s a shame that the WSJ takes direction from bank lobbyists.

On the contrary, some industry insiders blamed Trump’s $1.4B crypto profits as largely responsible for the ethics stand-off and the bill’s failure. 

SEC, CFTC advance crypto clarity via rulemaking

Here, it’s worth pointing out that the bill stalled on Tuesday. However, by Thursday, the regulators (SEC and CFTC) had begun rolling out rulemakings. 

Notably, the CFTC issued no-action relief for passive software providers, effectively allowing players like self-custodial wallets such as Phantom to avoid registering as brokers to offer derivative trading. 

Additionally, the CFTC submitted a new crypto market structure proposal for White House review. If approved, it would allow existing and unregistered crypto platforms to get approval for leveraged trading. This is the regulated pathway that Hyperliquid is betting on to gain U.S market entry. 

Separately, the SEC also made similar moves. It published a 5-year tokenization exemption program, allowing crypto platforms to facilitate tokenized stock trading. This would exempt some firms from registering as full securities exchanges. 

Still, the rulemaking approach can be reversed by the next administration if the rules aren’t codified by Congressional legislation. For his part, ETF expert Nate Geraci views the rulemaking as a “legitimate window” for the crypto industry to build. 

However, others believe that there are still regulatory risks for investors and developers if the next regime is anti-crypto. 

Final Summary

  • Coinbase CEO slammed WSJ for linking him to the CLARITY Act’s failure. 
  • Analysts are split on regulatory risks associated with SEC and CFTC’s rulemakings.

data.title: XRP vs Solana vs Cardano — Which altcoin will have the best September?
data.description:
Altcoin leverage remains below its risk threshold, according to crypto market intelligence platform Glassnode in a post on X.

When the altcoin market’s Open Interest comes to within a few percentage points of Bitcoin’s [BTC], the altcoin market can be considered overextended. As it stands though, these conditions are far from being met.

Now, some of the market’s most popular leading alts, Solana [SOL], Cardano [ADA], and Ripple [XRP], have had bullish runs in recent weeks. Which of them has the potential for the best returns for the rest of September?

All three alts showcase a bullish structure

Solana’s daily structure was flipped bullishly when the $98.41-swing level was breached. In recent weeks, SOL saw rejection from the $110-resistance area and briefly fell below $100.

The bulls were able to defend the $95-$100 demand zone and drove prices higher. The next resistance to watch is at $119.6, a former support turned resistance from late 2025.

Cardano has also been on a bullish run since its structure shift in July. The altcoin has set a series of higher highs since then. The retracement earlier this week saw ADA retest the $0.19-support level.

The reaction from there has been encouraging though, and Cardano may be primed to challenge the $0.23 and $0.255 resistance levels.

Like the other two, XRP also had a bullish structure at press time. Unlike the other two though, XRP was pushing into a long-term supply zone that has repeatedly driven the bulls back.

For this reason, it is possible that XRP would struggle to be the most bullish token among the three for the rest of the month.

Is Solana’s run done?

Solana has recorded the highest returns since Wednesday, around 16%, compared to 14% and 11% for Cardano and XRP. Additionally, only Solana has managed to breach the highs set towards the end of August, when Bitcoin began to pull back and dragged the altcoin market down with it.

This seemed to indicate that XRP and ADA have room to catch up to SOL, making them likely to return greater profits this month. And yet, it is Solana that has proven bullish momentum by making new local highs.

Therefore, so long as Bitcoin does not suffer a steep pullback, the leading altcoin among the trio, SOL, is likely to continue to register better returns.

Final Summary

  • Altcoin market leverage was relatively low compared to BTC’s Open Interest, indicating that altcoins still have room to make gains.
  • Among Solana, Cardano, and XRP, SOL appeared the most likely to continue its strong bullish momentum.

data.title: Altcoins are breaking out, but why isn’t anyone calling it an altseason yet?
data.description:
Altcoins have been stuck in the mud for what feels like forever. However, are things about to change in the near term?

Altcoins have waited two years for THIS!

The combined market cap of every coin outside the top 10 just broke above a trendline it’s been trapped under since late 2024.

And, it’s not been a small move either. In fact, the same is up over 10% this week, starting at about $199 billion to close near $220 billion.

Here, it’s worth noting that all this is happening on a support zone that’s held for about 1,000 days straight.

The timing is interesting too because crypto analyst AshCrypto mentioned on X that the four-year cycle usually treats 2026 as a bear phase. To its credit, Bitcoin’s holding up too, despite the failed Clarity Act vote and the Fed hiking rates.

The altcoins’ all-time high near $451 billion is still a long way off. No one’s calling it altseason yet.

On the other hand…

That’s not all either as at press time, Bitcoin dominance seemed to be forming what looks like a bearish descending triangle on the weekly charts.

If that breaks down, capital might just rotate out of Bitcoin and into everything else. Especially altcoins.

That might even be convenient timing because it would coincide with the breakout alts just noted.

There is a catch here though. CoinShares recently shared that Bitcoin’s stuck between a Fed that’s leaning hawkish and the CLARITY Act’s setback. According to the same, BTC won’t push decisively above $80K before year-end. Not unless inflation calms down or the Fed lowers its tone.

Here, what’s worth noting, however, is that Bitcoin is fairly insulated from the regulatory mess. On the contrary, altcoins like Ethereum [ETH] are far more exposed to it.

What’s holding it back?

For all the breakout talk, one metric refuses to collaborate. CoinMarketCap’s Altcoin Season Index was at 46 at press time; that’s Bitcoin territory.

It actually climbed up from 42 yesterday and 37 last week. Simply put, the direction is right. Just not the magnitude.

A reading below 75 doesn’t count as an altcoin season by CMC’s own definition. And, the index has been under that mark for months, nowhere near September 2025’s high of 78.

Final Summary

  • Altcoin market cap outside the top 10 broke a 2-year downtrend.
  • BTC.D looked bearish, but the altseason index is still at 46.

data.title: Bitcoin’s bullish phase is forming – But overbought conditions suggest…
data.description:
The crypto market is seeing a major shift in investors’ sentiment. In H2 2027, the digital assets market is experiencing bullish sentiments after failing to break through the long-standing resistance level in H1 2027.

According to CryptoQuant’s recent analysis, Bitcoin [BTC] is moving away from a weakness zone and toward a possible bullish phase. This conclusion was drawn based on Bitcoin’s bubble-versus-crash market structure indicator, which clearly showed that the extreme conditions associated with either a speculative bubble or a severe crash have faded.

Bitcoin has already gone through a period of correction/consolidation, but it has not yet experienced the kind of extreme speculative mania that historically marked major cycle tops. Therefore, the analyst believes BTC could still have room to enter a stronger upward trend.

As per CryptoQuant,

The full-fledged bullish rally has not yet begun. Currently, it is in the process of gradually approaching that stage.

Wall Street bets more on Bitcoin than gold

This comes as JPMorgan sheds light on the fact that institutional investors are more defensively positioned toward Bitcoin than gold. This, along with short interest and put options around Bitcoin ETFs such as BlackRock’s IBIT, now provides more downside protection.

The comparison with gold suggests Bitcoin currently has relatively heavier bearish hedging, while gold ETFs have recovered more of their 2026 outflows. Meanwhile, heavy put-option activity around Bitcoin ETFs indicates investors are protecting against downside. However, this does not necessarily mean they are outright bearish.

In other words, if BTC rallies, these hedges could be unwound, adding further buying pressure. This could in turn lead to a potential market impact of hedge unwinding and short covering worth $1 trillion.

Market dynamics paint a bearish picture

This comes as the price of Bitcoin was changing hands at $78,240.79 at press time after a hike of 2.5% in the past 24 hours. At the same time, the RSI was in the overbought zone, further creating a warning sign that bears might tend to pull the bulls back.

This happened along with the widening Bollinger Bands suggesting that Bitcoin is very volatile at the moment. Adding to the concern was AMBCrypto’s recent report that suggested that crypto’s Q4 outlook is turning cautious as the Fed’s 25 bps rate hike, rising Treasury yields, and a stronger U.S. dollar threaten liquidity and risk assets.

Final Summary

  • The extreme conditions associated with either a speculative bubble or a severe crash around Bitcoin have faded.
  • However, the RSI and Bollinger bands’ RSI suggest that bears might pull the bulls.

data.title: All about SKY’s price rally and if $569M in TVL growth will overshadow spot selling
data.description:
Sky Protocol [SKY] recorded significant gains over the last 24 hours, with the altcoin gaining by 14% on the charts. However, while these gains appeared to be strongly bullish, they have relied significantly on sentiment.

CoinMarketCap Sentiment, which uses a scale between -10 and 10 to measure investors’ outlook for an asset, highlighted a mildly bullish outlook for SKY. According to the same, it had a reading of 1.96, suggesting that investors are likely to accumulate more of the asset without the expectation of going all out.

Worth pointing out, however, that SKY’s perpetual market activity has been supporting these price gains too, with capital flows and positions pointing to further upside.

Capital flow and positions fuel bullish odds

SKY’s perpetual market revealed that there has been some growth in its capital base.

According to Coinglass, the Open Interest surged by 27% to hit roughly $39 million at press time. A surge in the capital base is a reflection of investors’ outlook for the asset, likely determining whether the asset trends higher or eventually sees a decline.

The Funding Rate, which tracks the cost of holding perpetual positions, rose too and pointed to growing long positioning in the market.

Are Spot traders selling?

Over the past three days, there has been an established selling trend among traders in the Spot market. In fact, there has been a cumulative sell-off of $363,000. This trend seemed to be even more visible over the last 24 hours, with Netflows of approximately $788,000.

For context, positive Netflows mean more SKY is moving into exchanges for sale than out of exchanges into private wallets for long-term holding.

As it stands, the primary concern stems from the divergence between Spot and Perpetual Market positioning.

In a typically sustained bull market, there tends to be bullish positioning from both the Spot and Perpetual Markets without overbought conditions. Spot would need to begin accumulating before the trend can be confirmed as fully supportive of a sustained bull market.

What do on-chain indicators tell us?

Finally, activity in the on-chain market has been fairly relaxed, without any major significant growth in market activity.

For instance, DeFiLlama reported that SKY’s Total Value Locked (TVL) has maintained a steady path with no significant gains or drops until 17th September. On that day, it added $569 million.

This growth, however, did not coincide with the fees generated as they held steady over the past day. Simply put, the price is now likely to continue its uptrend if market activity still supports it.

Final Summary

  • SKY gained by 14% as Open Interest climbed by 27% to $39 million.

  • Spot traders recorded $363,000 in cumulative selling over three days, creating a divergence between Spot and Perpetual market activity.

data.title: Can Ethereum turn Friday’s price rally of 6.5% into a sustained breakout?
data.description:
Ethereum [ETH] surged by 6.5% in the last 24 hours to trade at $2,618.67 at press time. This is a level the altcoin last saw back in January 2026. The timing here is interesting since the global cryptocurrency market cap also climbed to $2.88 trillion following gains of 4.6%. 

What is also interesting is that the said recovery followed several developments that would normally put significant pressure on risk assets.

For context, over the past week, the CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points. Additionally, the Bank of Japan also raised rates while the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) moved back above 100 and and oil prices increased.

Not just a price playdate

And yetm Ethereum saw a surge in whale transactions. This, and its holder base, continued to expand, with a record 207.17 million non-empty wallets. Staking is another major factor that has supported long-term ETH demand.

With more than 40 million ETH currently staked, there has been a significant removal of ETH from immediately available market supply. 

At the same time, Ethereum has remained a major hub for decentralized finance (DeFi), securing roughly $50 billion in TVL across lending platforms, decentralized exchanges, stablecoin applications and liquid-staking protocols. 

Finally, ETH ETFs also flipped the three-day outflow streak with $143.7 million in inflows. 

Other altcoins also surfed the bullish momentum

Needless to say, besides Ethereum, Bitcoin [BTC] moved back above $80,000, while several major altcoins recorded more significant gains.

For instance, Solana [SOL] and Hyperliquid [HYPE] hiked by more than 10% and Uniswap [UNI] gained by around 16%.

Is there still some uncertainty around?

However, not everything may be as rosy as it seems. The Ethereum Foundation transferred approximately $2.45 million worth of ETH to an unlabeled Gnosis Safe, a type of smart contract wallet commonly used for managing funds collectively or securely.

Now, because the receiving wallet is unlabeled, it is not yet clear whether it is directly controlled by the Ethereum Foundation or belongs to another entity.

The transfer, therefore, does not necessarily mean that the foundation is selling ETH or reducing its holdings. This, because on-chain data reportedly shows that the Foundation still holds around $235.46 million worth of ETH and $23 million in USDC.

Final Summary

  • Ethereum’s recent gains were recorded despite several negative developments that would have impacted its bullish momentum.
  • Besides ETH and BTC, several altcoins saw massive surges, with some seeing weekly hikes of over 45%.

data.title: Aptos jumps 18% as Layer 1 rotation accelerates – Is $0.825 next for APT?
data.description:
Aptos saw a price increase of 18.6% as Layer-1 rotation accelerated, strengthening the recovery profile as the higher-beta altcoins attracted speculative demand.

APT’s impulse move emerged alongside the broader strength across the Layer-1 tokens, instead of an isolated, specific catalyst. 

Notably, several assets within this category also recorded double-digit gains as market participants shifted toward higher-beta assets.

Therefore, APT’s price increase highlighted a broader change in market participation toward the Layer-1 sector. 

At the time of press, the token traded around the $0.6616 area after buyers heightened their activity during the latest session. Therefore, the sector rotation helped APT recover from its previous consolidation range. 

Top traders leaned firmly toward APT longs

The Binance top traders on the other side maintained a clear long-side bias as APT pushed towards its range ceiling. Accordingly, the long accounts accounted for 61.79%, against the shorts at 8.21%.

The Binance Top Trader Long/Short Ratio as a result reached 1.62, keeping positioning leaning toward the bulls. 

Notably, the ratio had fluctuated substantially earlier, including a rapid spike around the September 11 period.

The latest reading however still suggested more top trader accounts betting on upside than downside. 

Additionally, the positioning also complemented the Layer-1 rotation already supporting the token’s spot-market recovery.

Noteworthy, the long dominance also raised the importance of APT successfully holding its breakout attempt. This is because a price rejection could expose those bullish positions if traders reduce leverage after the rapid rally.

Can APT finally escape its range?

Looking at the daily timeframe chart, Aptos [APT] spent months oscillating between the $0.509 and $0.654 price range, struggling around the range ceiling repeatedly. 

The recent attempts also introduced candle wicks above the $0.654 level, reflecting notable liquidity sweeps before price probably retraces lower.

The latest price advance however carried APT back above that boundary, with price reaching approximately $0.660 on the daily timeframe chart. 

The most recent session, as of press time, also hit a $0.711 high, extending into liquidity resting above the established price range.

Unlike previous attempts, the bulls now need acceptance above the $0.654 level instead of another temporary wick beyond the resistance level. 

Meanwhile, the RSI indicator had climbed to 60.94, remaining below overbought territory while strengthening above its 53.83 average. Additionally, the MACD indicator also supported the bulls after crossing above its signal line.

Strongly holding that level would reinforce the technical breakout structure and could shift attention toward the $0.825 price resistance.

Liquidity sweep leaves Aptos facing two paths

More importantly, the technical chart highlighted that APT had already grabbed liquidity above its long-standing $0.654 range ceiling.

Notably, the push toward $0.711 reached the same upper region where previous liquidity sweeps had emerged on the Binance Liquidation Heatmap.

The heatmap strengthened that interpretation, since APT price had already moved through considerable overhead liquidity during its sharp expansion. 

However, additional liquidation clusters remained higher, particularly around the $0.69 to $0.72 area.

A persistent hold above $0.654 establishing support would keep those remaining upper clusters relevant and likely support another liquidity-driven extension.

Beyond that zone, the $0.825 level would introduce the next key technical resistance from the daily structure.

Another failure however above the $0.654 zone would change the immediate risk picture greatly. Also, lower liquidation liquidity remained notable around the $0.63 to $0.60 area, giving price potential downside pulls.

Ultimately, a deeper price reversal could eventually expose the broader $0.509 range floor, especially if the bullish leverage unwind after the rally.

Final Summary

  • APT’s 18.6% rally pushed price beyond $0.654 while top traders favored longs.
  • A sustained holding above $0.654 could target remaining upper liquidity; rejection exposes $0.63–$0.60.

data.title: NEAR rallies 24% after AI utility expands across 43 models – Is rally built to last?
data.description:
NEAR has emerged as the top-performing AI crypto token, surging 24.52% as activity expanded across the trading markets and its confidential infrastructure.

Reportedly, the confidential TVL recently surpassed $70 million, triggering the network’s first milestone snapshot under its incentive program. Notably, the program allocated 333,333 milestone tokens, reinforcing participation surrounding the Confidential Intents ecosystem.

Accordingly, these tokens are to remain locked until NEAR’s three-day volume-weighted average price reaches at least $3.33. 

Importantly, NEAR’s price climbed beyond the program’s $3.33 threshold during the expansion. However, eligibility requires its three-day volume-weighted average price to remain at least $3.33 before unlocking.

Beyond incentives, the protocol’s Confidential Intents supported private execution across more than 30 connected blockchains. Additionally, NEAR had also linked Intents with autonomous-agent infrastructure for asset transfers and cross-chain payments.

Furthermore, the token’s AI utility expanded further through staking-based computing credits covering 43 AI models. Meanwhile, spot volume also surged 131.81% to $1.63 billion, suggesting a broader market participation behind the most recent price increase.

Whale orders deepen spot demand

Large market participants strengthened NEAR’s demand picture as price accelerated. CryptoQuant’s Spot Average Order Size registered Big Whale Orders, indicating larger transactions.

Meanwhile, the 90-day Spot Taker CVD remained Taker Buy Dominant. That reading indicated aggressive buyers controlled executed Spot activity during the rally.

However, whale-sized orders alone did not prove accumulation. The Taker Buy Dominant reading provided stronger evidence that active demand accompanied those trades. This combination gave NEAR’s move firmer Spot-market support.

Leverage builds behind NEAR’s rally

By contrast, NEAR’s derivatives market expanded sharply as traders increased exposure.

Open Interest rose 39.54% to $924.66 million. Derivatives Volume surged 101.79% to $1.85 billion. The expansion could support continuation while buyers defended the breakout.

However, elevated leverage also increased liquidation risk if NEAR reversed sharply.

Crucially, Spot buying and Big Whale Orders accompanied this derivatives expansion. Leverage therefore amplified identifiable demand instead of carrying the rally alone.

Can NEAR price reach $4?

During its price uptrend, NEAR broke decisively above the $2.820 level, extending its recovery beyond a resistance level that previously rejected further price advance.

Price subsequently hit the $3.461level, bringing the higher-timeframe Fair Value Gap (FVG) into immediate focus. Particularly, the imbalance stretched approximately between the $3.65 and $4.20 range, which placed $4.00 inside the target region.

Furthermore, the directional strength had intensified substantially during the breakout with the ADX reaching 55.6278, while +DI at 50.3812 overwhelming -DI at 4.1701.

Also, the Parabolic SAR indicator at $2.297 remained below the prevailing market price, reinforcing the development of bullish technical structure. Therefore, NEAR could extend deeper into the FVG if the bulls maintain control above the $2.820 zone.

Alternatively, rejection from the imbalance could likely send the price toward the breakout zone before another recovery attempt.

Final Summary

  • NEAR’s 24.52% surge gained support from whale orders and aggressive spot buying.
  • NEAR’s breakout into the higher-timeframe FVG could shift attention toward the $4 region.

data.title: Polkadot: Assessing if ETF and network activity can carry DOT to $1.30
data.description:
Polkadot [DOT] is up by more than 13% in the past 24 hours. Similarly, the total crypto market is rallying as short liquidations increased by 17% to around $272 million.

But DOT’s surge is not only dependent on the broader crypto market strength. High network activity, capital inflows through treasury and ETFs, and a bullish technical outlook have been key.

Why is Polkadot surging?

Looking at the network activity, Polkadot‘s Monthly Active Addresses have doubled in September. The number has grown from 40K in August to a high of 82.9K, but the figures have since retraced to 80.3K.

Moreover, the monthly token trading volume has increased by 116%, hitting $4.70 billion.

Transactions have also continued to stay high, aligning with the past analysis. Daily transactions are averaging 238K, with the sum for the past 30 days at 7.20 million, as per Token Terminal.

In terms of capital flow, it turned positive this month on an overall scale.

For instance, 21Shares Polkadot ETF [TDOT] saw net inflows of $663K after two months of dormancy, as per SoSoValue. This indicated institutions were gradually returning to buying TDOT, which could be accelerated by the SEC’s regulatory clarity on tokenization.

Additionally, Treasury net flows turned positive after staying negative for 5 days this week. In the past 24 hours, net flows surpassed $2.04 million, 10 times bigger than the other positive day of the week.

Still, the weekly treasury net flows remain negative, at around $1.59 million.

Can bulls flip $1.30 into support?

Technically, Polkadot was respecting a rising trendline support on the daily timeframe. The price had bounced off the support for the third time and the altcoin appeared to be headed toward $1.30.

The Bollinger Bands (BB) were expanding, indicating volatility was increasing. Additionally, the Stochastic RSI with a reading of 30 was rebounding from the oversold territory. This hinted at seller exhaustion.

Flipping the $1.30-$1.44 zone into support would expose $1.70 and levels above $2.

On the other hand, a breakdown of the slanting trendline would invalidate the uptrend, especially losing $0.945 as horizontal support. This $0.945 level was the previous higher high (HH) in the ongoing uptrend.

Therefore, the market structure of Polkadot remains bullish unless the current pattern of HH and higher lows (HL) is lost.

Final Summary

  • Polkadot surged over 13% in the past 24 hours, amid high network activity, capital inflows and a bullish outlook. 
  • DOT price is respecting a rising trendline supporting further appreciation unless the price breaks below it.
